prompt: A friend messages you late at night saying today was awful, with a crying emoji. Your first reaction is—

options.text: Immediately call her, cheer her up first and then talk
Stay and chat with her, not saying anything heavy on the surface, but constantly thinking about how upset she is
Ask clearly what happened and try to help her sort things out
First judge whether it’s worth being that upset, then decide whether to get involved

prompt: At the beginning of a gathering, people aren’t familiar yet and the atmosphere feels a bit awkward. You usually—

options.text: Find a concrete topic, like food or plans, and steadily keep the conversation going
Don’t rush to blend in, only talk to people you feel comfortable with
Observe others first, then join in slowly when it feels right
Take the initiative to start topics, even if it’s a bit noisy, just to warm things up

prompt: You’ve been misunderstood, and the other person has even told others. You are more likely to—

options.text: Explain immediately, not wanting the awkwardness to linger
Say “forget it” on the surface, but replay it in your mind over and over
Sort out the whole situation and explain only the key facts
Not bother explaining, thinking people who misunderstand you aren’t important anyway

prompt: When making an important decision, you rely most on—

options.text: A strong but hard-to-explain inner feeling
Real-time interaction, others’ feedback, and changes in atmosphere
Your judgment of people and situations, especially who is trustworthy
Rules, logic, risks, and probability of success

prompt: When you like someone, your most likely state is—

options.text: Naturally finding ways to talk to her and create chances to be noticed
No obvious change outwardly, but secretly amplifying your feelings
Quietly remembering her needs and taking care of her through actions
Treating her obviously differently from others, and not hiding favoritism

prompt: Your most comfortable working state is—

options.text: Setting your own pace and making your own decisions, not liking interference
When your mood is right, efficiency is high; when it’s not, it drops suddenly
Working while talking; a lively environment doesn’t affect you
Having clear processes, standards, and correct answers makes you feel secure

prompt: If you were guiding a newcomer, you would be more like—

options.text: Constantly encouraging her so she doesn’t feel nervous
Able to sense her unease, but not necessarily pointing it out directly
Carefully teaching steps and principles so she can get started quickly
First observing her potential before deciding how much effort to invest

prompt: When you’re under a lot of pressure, you are more like—

options.text: Start making lists and finding solutions, reorganizing the chaos
Still try to keep the atmosphere lively so others won’t worry
Become a bit colder, not wanting to explain or be disturbed
Say you’re fine, but actually overthink and feel worse when alone

prompt: If someone cries hard in front of you, you are most likely to—

options.text: Hand her tissues and water, and try to cheer her up a little
Sit beside her quietly, not rushing or pushing her to stop
Wait until she calms down, then help her figure out what to do
Feel a bit impatient, thinking too much emotional release is pointless

prompt: Which sentence best describes your way of handling things—

options.text: First judge whether it’s worth investing; if not, I won’t keep wasting energy
Fix the atmosphere first; everything else will work out somehow
I have a lot of feelings, but I’m not good at expressing them
If something can be explained clearly, don’t leave it to guesswork

prompt: If people say you’re “a bit hard to understand,” it’s most likely because—

options.text: You’re actually warm, but sometimes come off as too energetic or loud
You seem indifferent, but internally you replay and magnify details
You speak too logically, like solving problems instead of comforting people
You can be sharp with unimportant people, but very protective of your own

prompt: What kind of person moves you the most—

options.text: Someone reliable, steady, and serious, who makes you feel at ease
Someone independent and strong, yet willing to be specially cherished by you
Someone who matches your energy and enjoys being lively with you
Someone who understands your unspoken emotions and takes the initiative

prompt: After moving to a new place with many shops and restaurants nearby, you are more likely to—

options.text: Walk in on impulse depending on your mood, remembering both good and bad experiences
Ask companions for opinions, trying to find something everyone likes
Take your time, observe first, and try places that feel right to you
Check reviews or ask for recommendations before deciding

prompt: If someone suddenly disrupts your planned schedule, you usually—

options.text: Feel a bit unhappy but quietly adapt
Point out the issue directly and demand a more reasonable solution
Seem calm on the surface, but hold onto dissatisfaction for a long time
Accept it and come up with a new plan that works for everyone

prompt: When facing unfamiliar software, devices, or rules, you are more like—

options.text: Study the rules first, then get up to speed efficiently
Start using it based on your own understanding and figure things out later
Learn it yourself first, then help others learn it too
Learn and use it at your own pace, not worrying much about efficiency or rules

prompt: If you care deeply about someone, you are more likely to—

options.text: Keep boundaries with others, but slowly show dependence only to her
Not say sweet words, but quietly stand on her side
Feel your emotions deepen to the point you can’t easily pull away
Can’t help but take care of her—worrying about her eating, sleeping, and being treated well

prompt: In a group, your usual role is—

options.text: Noticing who’s tired, falling behind, or needs care
Not necessarily the most active, but having your own pace and boundaries
Someone who makes decisions, pushes things forward, and gets things done
Quiet, but deeply observant and emotionally aware

prompt: If someone is treated unfairly, your reaction is—

options.text: Observe calmly before taking action
Stand up directly, even if the other person is stronger
Feel the injustice deeply and carry it emotionally for a long time
Protect the person first, then deal with the situation

prompt: Which kind of environment makes you feel most comfortable—

options.text: A space for solitude, where intense emotions and inspiration can exist
A slower pace with flowers, light, and your own familiar little world
Safe, warm, lively, with everyone well taken care of
Efficient and organized, where everything has its place and rules

prompt: What people misunderstand about you most easily is—

options.text: They think you’re lazy, but you’re just slow-paced and take time to warm up
They think you’re too strong, but you just dislike chaos and unfairness
They think you’re cold, but you just don’t show your emotions easily
They think you’re easygoing, but you’re actually very firm when protecting others

prompt: How do you usually express liking someone—

options.text: By showing “I’m on your side” rather than saying sweet words
By turning it into everyday care through small actions
By quietly getting closer, occasionally acting cute—but only with special people
By becoming deeply attached, almost unable to pull yourself away

prompt: If a child nearby suddenly throws a tantrum, you are most likely to—

options.text: Crouch down and stay with them, waiting patiently for them to calm down
Explain the rules clearly so they understand boundaries
Feel a bit flustered inside, but remain calm on the outside
Naturally pick them up, comfort them, and handle everything

prompt: What bothers you most at work is—

options.text: Focusing only on efficiency while ignoring people’s well-being
Lack of emotion, aesthetics, creativity, or fun
Being constantly rushed, interrupted, and unable to keep your own pace
Knowing there’s a better way, but no one is willing to implement it

prompt: Which sentence feels most like you—

options.text: It’s okay to fall behind—just live at your own pace
Say what needs to be said, and stand your ground when necessary
The deepest love is often hidden in silence
Anyone I truly care about, I will protect with all my heart
